messages:
incident-bot: Pager: high tail latency observed for hosted text generation in us-west-1 (>95th pctl). Alerts triggered 6887654321. Paging on-call.
jen: taking this — oncall. Kicking off quick triage. ETA 5m for initial findings.
kevin: thanks jen. any customer-facing impact yet? volume of errors?
maria: seeing elevated token latency and some 504s from prod-gen behind the loadbalancer. ~2% of requests failing in last 2m, tail latency 8-12s.
jen: ok. immediate mitigation: can we shift traffic from us-west-1 to us-west-2 for critical routes? ops-bot, can you assess capacity?
ops-bot: running capacity check... us-west-2 spare capacity is available for burst, but backend models on us-west-2 are on a different quantized build; small perf delta expected. Recommend routing only critical-tier traffic.
kevin: agree. meanwhile we should prepare a status update. I'll draft initial copy.
kevin: DRAFT for status page (please review):\n---\nWe are investigating elevated request latency and intermittent failures for text generation services in US West (us-west-1). Some requests may experience slow responses or transient timeouts. Our on-call is actively triaging and we will provide updates every 30 minutes or as we have significant changes.\nCustomer impact: ~2% requests may be affected, primarily in us-west-1.\nMitigation: traffic rerouting and service rollbacks are being evaluated.\n---\nPlease flag any wording issues.
maria: can we add a note to avoid implying data loss? Legal may want to review phrasing about impact.
legal: quick note — avoid "failures" -> use "intermittent timeouts"; avoid definitive root-cause language. Also add link to status page and support contact.
kevin: updated: \n---\nWe are investigating elevated request latency and intermittent timeouts for text generation services in US West (us-west-1). Some requests may experience slow responses or transient timeouts. Our on-call team is actively triaging; updates every 30 minutes.\nCustomer impact: Approximately 2% of requests may be experiencing increased latency or timeouts, primarily from us-west-1.\nMitigation: Traffic rerouting and service configuration rollbacks are being evaluated; we may route critical-tier requests to alternate regions.\nFor support, please contact support@redwood.ai or visit https://status.redwood.ai\n---\njen: looks good. Alex, want to do the publish and tag infra/eng-sre folks?
alex: publishing now. Will include affected component tags and ETA for next update 30m. Pushing initial update to status page.
statuspage-bot: Initial status update published: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/rdw-8472 - "Investigating: Elevated latency in US West". (6887654390)
maria: routing changes started at 6887654405 — shifting critical-tier traffic to us-west-2. Monitoring impact.
jen: thanks. watching error rate.
ops-bot: reroute applied for critical tier. error rate for critical down from 2.1% -> 0.3% in last 60s.
kevin: preparing next update: note that mitigation reduced customer impact for critical-tier; still investigating root cause and broader rollback plan.
kevin: UPDATE (30m):\n---\nWe mitigated impact for critical customers by routing critical-tier traffic to an alternate region. We continue to investigate the cause of elevated tail latency in us-west-1 and are evaluating rollback and configuration changes. Non-critical traffic may still experience elevated latency.\nNext update: 30 minutes or sooner as we have new info.\n---\nalex: posted update (6887656145). statuspage-bot link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/rdw-8472/updates/2
maria: found correlation between recent kernel patch on a subset of inference hosts and increased context switch rates — digging deeper. No evidence of data loss.
legal: good that there's no data loss; hold final wording on root cause until we confirm. suggest phrasing: "preliminary investigation shows correlation".
kevin: will use "preliminary analysis indicates a correlation" in next update.
jen: we should prepare a resolved note if we roll back kernel patch and metrics normalize. Ops, can you stage rollback for a gradual canary?
ops-bot: canary rollback scheduled 6887657000. will observe for 5 minutes then expand.
maria: rollback canary showed improvement — tail latency back to baseline for canary hosts. expanding rollback across cluster now.
ops-bot: rollback complete across us-west-1 at 6887657370. tail latency normalized. Error rates back to baseline.
kevin: RESOLVED DRAFT:\n---\nResolved: We have rolled back a recent kernel patch on affected inference hosts in US West (us-west-1) which restored normal latency and response rates. Our preliminary analysis indicates the patch correlated with increased context-switch overhead on a subset of hosts. No customer data was compromised.\nIf you continue to see issues, please contact support@redwood.ai. We will follow up with a post-incident report that includes timeline and remediation plan.\n---\nlegal: fine to publish with "preliminary analysis indicates" wording. please avoid granular host counts in public note.
alex: publishing resolved notice now. statuspage-bot: Resolved update published: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/rdw-8472/updates/3 (6887654723)
jen: thanks team. filing post-incident task to eng-ml for follow-up and rollback automation.
kevin: closing thread here — will attach PIR once ready. :thumbsup:
